name: John Wallis
summary: Seventeenth-century Anglican minister, Savilian Professor of Geometry at Oxford, and contributor to mathematics, natural philosophy, and theology.

name: University of Oxford
summary: Historic university in England where Wallis served as Savilian Professor of Geometry.

name: Emmanuel College, Cambridge
summary: College at the University of Cambridge known for training Puritan ministers, where Wallis matriculated.

name: Royal Society
summary: Scientific academy founded in 1660, of which Wallis was a founder member.

name: Arithmetica infinitorum
summary: Wallis's 1655 algebraic work famous for the Wallis product and infinite series methods.

name: Mechanica
summary: Wallis's three-part treatise on mathematical physics and laws of motion published between 1669 and 1671.

name: Theological Discourses
summary: Collection of eight letters by Wallis published in 1692 defending the doctrine of the Trinity.

name: Isaac Newton
summary: Physicist and mathematician whose development of calculus was influenced by Wallis's work.

name: Thomas Hobbes
summary: Philosopher and rival of Wallis who disputed with him on mathematics and theology.

name: Christopher Wren
summary: Fellow of the Royal Society who, with Wallis and Huygens, wrote treatises on laws of motion in 1668.

name: Christiaan Huygens
summary: Mathematician and Fellow of the Royal Society who contributed to laws of motion alongside Wallis.

name: Henry Oldenburg
summary: Secretary of the Royal Society who corresponded with Wallis regarding natural philosophy.

name: Oxford Philosophical Society
summary: Group modelled on the Royal Society, presided over by Wallis during the 1680s.

name: Church of England
summary: State church to which Wallis conformed after the Restoration.
